problem: Existing adversarial attacks on VLN mostly assume white-box gradient access and are costly. Prior black-box attacks (ZOO, NES, SimBA) target single-step decisions and cannot handle VLN's delayed feedback, error accumulation and policy self-correction.
motivation: Deployed VLN agents are proprietary, so robustness must be assessed from observable inputs and outputs only. The attack must account for long-term behavioral effects over a multi-step perception-action loop, and final metrics like SR, SPL and NE are near-binary for short instructions and give sparse optimization signal.
key_idea: Use a dual-granularity behavior feedback (trajectory-level score, action-level probability-margin reward, deviation indicator) to drive a gradient-free hybrid search that adaptively accumulates Perlin-noise intensity and genetically evolves the noise structure.
insight: Behavior feedback matters most at the action level. Ablation: action-only feedback reaches 45.74% ASR vs 30.85% for trajectory-only and 23.40% for random search, and the full feedback gets 47.87%. Adaptive update and structure evolution are complementary: each alone gives 38.30% / 26.60% ASR vs 47.87% together. Perlin noise alone is not enough, since Perlin with NES/Bayes/SimBA gets 39.33/19.10/20.22% ASR vs 47.87%, so the gains come from the framework. HAMT is more vulnerable to occlusion while MapGPT is more vulnerable to global noise.
method: Perlin-noise perturbation: a single universal perturbation delta (L-inf bounded) applied to every first-person frame, parameterized by a few Perlin parameters to simulate haze/dust and keep the search low-dimensional
Trajectory-level score G: lambda*Norm(dNE) - (1-lambda)*Norm(dSPL) relative to the clean run, with lambda=0.5
Action-level reward R: sum over steps of (probability of the most likely wrong action minus probability of the reference action), capturing 'soft failures' when the trajectory is unchanged
Deviation indicator gamma: binary flag for whether the trajectory deviates from the reference; gates whether gain uses G (gamma=1) or R (gamma=0)

Adaptive perturbation update: candidates are added to the cumulative base noise with a fixed step alpha and sign; best positive-gain candidate is chosen with trajectory-deviation candidates prioritized; if none improves, keep the base and flip the sign
Population evolutionary refinement: top-k=2 parents by the gamma-aware ranking, crossover, mutation (0.2), deduplication and random resampling; population 10, 20 rounds

setting.backbone: Attack targets: HAMT (official R2R weights), MapGPT with Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct or GPT-4V. Attacker itself is gradient-free search.
setting.training_data: none (attack is optimized per instruction at test time via query access; victim models are used as released)
setting.observation: Panoramic first-person RGB views perturbed by Perlin noise; attacker sees action probabilities and final navigation metrics
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph viewpoints plus STOP (victim agents)
setting.privileged: Query access to output action probabilities and navigation metrics, plus the clean-run reference trajectory and goal (for SPL/NE/ASR); no gradients or internals

numbers.extra: black-box attack, up to 20 rounds, population 10; ASR is attack success rate, SPL/NE are under attack (lower SPL / higher NE = stronger attack); clean HAMT SPL 57.69, NE 3.94

numbers_note: Numbers are attack results (ASR, and victim SPL/NE under attack), not navigation-agent performance. The ablation table uses a 165-instruction HAMT subset (full method ASR 47.87, SPL 25.95, NE 5.52).
results: AdvNav reaches 49.70% ASR on HAMT, lowering SPL from 57.69 to 29.35 and raising NE from 3.94 to 6.05 m. It beats the strongest baseline, Mask Occlusion (Bayes), at 38.74% ASR. On MapGPT it reaches 65.96% (Qwen3-VL) and 87.30% (GPT-4V) ASR vs the best baseline Gaussian Noise (NES) at 58.76% and 76.92%. Cost is about 6.77 rounds at ~32 s each and 2.4 GB GPU memory, with lower LPIPS than the baselines.
limitations: Evaluated only on R2R in a discrete Matterport3D simulator with two victim models, and MapGPT on a 165-instruction subset; no real-world or continuous-environment tests
Baselines are self-built black-box variants rather than published VLN attacks; per-instruction online optimization needs many queries and reference-trajectory access
No defenses or adversarial-training evaluation; the perturbation is a digital Perlin overlay, not physically realized
